newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian stocks battered, no further erosion seen.
newsitem.headline: Croatian stocks battered, no further erosion seen.

text.p: Croatian stocks took another battering on Thursday with nearly all active issues falling, but analysts predicted no further erosion after considerable recent losses almost across the board.
"Share prices have already fallen a lot. They have now probably reached resistance," Davor Relja of Split's brokerage Faktor told Reuters by telephone.
Turnover doubled to 6.8 million kuna but volume rose very slightly to 5,892 shares. Twelve of fifteen active issues fell, two rose and one was flat.
"Trade is extremely poor with prices lower than they have been in over six months," said Velimir Zelimorski, trader at Fima brokers.
"There is no long-term buying in such an unstable market, everyone is speculating," he added.
Fully-listed Zagrebacka Banka ordinaries were the most active, accounting for one third of the trade with 2,891 ordinary shares sold. It rose 30 kuna or 1.5 percent to close at 2,030 kuna.
Its preferred E-series stock slid 30 kuna to 1,170 on volume of 106 units but traders expected it to stabilise.
Another blue chip drugs company Pliva ended flat at the top of today's 441-450 kuna traded range.
Food processor Podravka continued its slide, closing four kuna lower at 265 kuna after selling 1,019 units at 240-269.9 kuna.
Chocolate maker Kras edged down 0.10 kuna to 409.9 on volume of 661.
"Kras may get an ISO quality certificate very soon which could bring about some increase in its price, though nothing very significant," said Relja.
Bigger of the two gainers was Karlovacka Pivovara brewery, adding 20 kuna or 6.45 percent to 330 kuna on volume of 188.
Hotelier Suncani Hvar led the day's losers. It dipped 5.26 percent to 54 kuna with 385 shares changing hands.
Three other tourist firms were also on the losing side but most market participants foresee a recovery of tourism trade as likely to boost hotelier prices in medium term.
Rab's Hoteli Imperial closed at 170 kuna on volume of 28 shares in a first deal since last November, one kuna below its recent price on an over-the-counter market in Varazdin.
